system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:45:20 UTC, ivy.chen's PowerShell process, launched from Explorer at medium integrity, ran Compress-Archive on \\FILE-NWD-01\Shared\Clients and wrote C:\Users\ivy.chen\AppData\Local\Temp\c.zip. The archive was created at 13:45:24 UTC.

At 13:50:50 UTC, a proxy tunnel from WS-ICHEN-01 to quickshare-drop.net carried 51,000,000 client-to-server bytes; the corresponding Zeek connection records 50,100,389 client-originated bytes. This is consistent with a large outbound transfer to an unapproved file-sharing destination.
The large proxy connection was attributed by Windows Filtering Platform and Sysmon to Chrome process 4120 running as ivy.chen.

The archive creation shortly before the large transfer, together with the transfer to a file-sharing service not included among the organization's approved services, strongly supports deliberate staging and exfiltration of client data.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy and Zeek records provide connection byte counts and destination, but do not expose the upload request, remote object name, or transferred content.
The available records do not directly tie the contents of c.zip to the later transfer; their relationship is strongly suggested by timing but not proven.
The evidence provided covers a limited time window and does not establish the full scope or duration of activity.
claims_not_established: The exact contents, size, and sensitivity of c.zip are not established.
The identity of the quickshare-drop.net account or recipient, and whether the upload completed and remained accessible, are not established.
The evidence does not establish whether ivy.chen acted knowingly or whether her account or session was compromised.
additional_evidence_needed: Collect the c.zip file, its metadata and hash, and relevant filesystem or endpoint telemetry to determine its contents and provenance.
Obtain detailed proxy or network records for the quickshare-drop.net session, including request method, URL, response status, and any available upload or object identifiers.
Review browser, identity-provider, and endpoint evidence for account/session compromise and determine whether ivy.chen authorized the transfer.
Preserve and review relevant quickshare-drop.net and cloud-account records to identify the recipient, subsequent access, and any additional transfers.
